title: Rabbi Yosi Barʾ
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned under this name in [Yerushalmi Berakhot, chapter 8, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.8.1.5), where he says: ‘They are accustomed there, in a place where there is no wine,’ etc. The saying is cited in [Tosafot, Pesachim 106b](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Pesachim.106b), in the comment beginning ‘Mekadesh,’ where the name is Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Bun. Hyman holds that the earlier abbreviation was undoubtedly בר״ב, meaning ‘son of Rabbi Bun’; the bet subsequently dropped out, leaving בר׳. He is likewise mentioned by this name in Demai, chapter 2, at the end of halakhah 1.[^1]

notes.text: Barʾ retains the shortened patronymic בר׳ that Hyman seeks to explain. Tosafot reads “Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Bun,” whereas the Yerushalmi reads “Rabbi Yosi Beribi.” Hyman’s lost-bet reconstruction is his proposed explanation.
